lines.trans: CEO Byun? Hello—right outside my apartment? Got it.
I will just leave right now.
Stay put for now—I will go hear what she has to say and come back.
How did you know where my apartment is?
Do you not remember, Producer Ra? I came here once five years ago too.
By any chance, do you know anything about this incident, Producer Ra?
How would someone like me know?
Since you direct the show Cindy stars in, I will lay it right on the table—our Cindy went into hiding.
She never once acted like this before, yet lately it is as if late puberty hit—she is giving me headaches.
Well, as long as the rumors are untrue, that is the end of it.

meanings.note: Used as numeral + counter (5년).

examples.text: 기억 안 나, 라 피디? 5년 전에도 여기 한번 온 적 있었는데.
examples.trans: Do you not remember, Producer Ra? I came here once five years ago too.
This point about five years is really important.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: used before a verb to tell someone to stop an ongoing action

examples.trans: Stop worrying now.
I'm so full I'll stop eating.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 취해서 거짓말을 좀 했는데 준모 선배님이 기억을 하나 못하나 알아내야 한다는 말씀이시죠?
examples.trans: So you told some lies while drunk, and I must find out whether Senior Joon-mo remembers them or not, right?
Here the word for 'memory' is key.

meanings.note: Used as idiomatic connective (까놓고).

examples.text: 라 피디는 우리 신디가 출연하고 있는 프로그램 피디니까 내가 톡 까놓고 말할게. 우리 신디 지금 잠수 탔어요.
examples.trans: Since you direct the show Cindy stars in, I will lay it right on the table—our Cindy went into hiding.
Let us do that (laying cards out and) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: verb regarding

examples.trans: About this.
Treat people.

meanings.note: Used as adverbial -게 (뒤늦게).

examples.text: 한 번도 이런 적 없던 애인데 요새 뒤늦게 사춘기가 온 건지 좀 속을 썩이네.
examples.trans: She never once acted like this before, yet lately it is as if late puberty hit—she is giving me headaches.
It is really belatedly compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.

meanings.note: Common verb for expressing thoughts in words.

examples.trans: Please speak slowly.
Speak loudly.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used as noun + dative (사건에).

examples.text: 혹시 이 사건에 대해서 우리 라 피디 아는 거 있어요?
examples.trans: By any chance, do you know anything about this incident, Producer Ra?
This point about incident is really important.

meanings.en: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
meanings.note: adverbial use of the noun 사실 (fact)

examples.trans: Honestly, I don't know well either.
In fact, I couldn't sleep yesterday.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 얘 요새 왜 이렇게 반항해? 사춘기야?
examples.trans: Why is this kid rebelling like this lately—did he hit puberty?
Here the word for 'is it puberty?' is key.
Did you hear about this stomach, insides?
I was busy today because of stomach, insides.

meanings.note: Used as idiomatic exclamatory -네 (썩이네.).

examples.text: 한 번도 이런 적 없던 애인데 요새 뒤늦게 사춘기가 온 건지 좀 속을 썩이네.
examples.trans: She never once acted like this before, yet lately it is as if late puberty hit—she is giving me headaches.
Let us do that (is worrying me) right away.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: noun

examples.trans: Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Used only when answering or checking a phone call, not in person.

examples.trans: Hello? Who is this?
Hello, can you hear me?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 요사이

examples.trans: How have you been doing these days?
I have too much work lately.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
Test
Test2

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as polite imperative (있어봐요,).

examples.text: 일단 있어봐요, 내가 가서 뭔 얘긴지 듣고 올 테니까.
examples.trans: Stay put for now—I will go hear what she has to say and come back.
Let us do that (stay put) right away.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun (잠수).

examples.trans: What does it look like? Have none of you ever gone off the grid before?

examples.text: 아니, 지금 퇴원하다가 잠수를 타는 거야? 근데 왜 이 차를 타?
examples.trans: Wait, you are going into hiding right out of the hospital? Why get into this car, though?

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 신디 1박 2일 출연한다고 발표하고 나서 우리 주식 하한가야!
examples.trans: Right after we announced Cindy was appearing on 2 Days & 1 Night, our stock hit rock bottom!
This expression comes from 'that she will appear'.

meanings.note: intransitive verb; also means 'to ride' in another sense

examples.text: 불을 줄이지 않으면 고기가 다 타요.
examples.trans: If you don't lower the heat, the meat will burn completely.
Firewood is burning brightly in the stove.
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

meanings.note: Used as mimetic adverb (톡).

examples.text: 라 피디는 우리 신디가 출연하고 있는 프로그램 피디니까 내가 톡 까놓고 말할게. 우리 신디 지금 잠수 탔어요.
examples.trans: Since you direct the show Cindy stars in, I will lay it right on the table—our Cindy went into hiding.
I thought it over again (openly, bluntly).

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Written as one word (한번) when softening a suggestion or request ('why don't we...').

examples.trans: Try eating this food.
Come visit sometime when you have time.

meanings.note: Softens a question or expresses uncertainty.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
Do you happen to have time?
